title: I started building a news app when I was a teenager because I was tired of missing the stories that actually mattered.
body:
It felt like the news industry was stuck in a loop. You either had to scroll through endless noise to find one useful fact, or you were fed an algorithmically curated feed that felt more like an echo chamber than a window into the world. I wanted something different.

I realized that the problem was not a lack of information. We have more information than ever. The problem was the signal to noise ratio. Most apps are designed to keep you clicking, not to help you understand what is happening.

Building Headlinne meant rethinking how we consume information from the ground up. We decided to use AI not to guess what you want to see, but to act as a personal editor that cuts through the clutter. It is about giving you the substance you need to form your own opinions, without the fluff or the rage bait.

It has been a long road from that first prototype to where we are now. But the goal remains the same. We are building a tool that respects your time and your intelligence.
cta: If you are tired of the noise, you can see how we are changing the way people read the news at HEADLINNE.com.
